questions.question: Which queue has strict priority over the Macrotask (Task) queue in the JavaScript Event Loop?
options: Microtask Queue
Render Animation Queue
I/O Polling Queue
Worker Message Queue
questions.explanation: After each synchronous frame completes on the call stack, the JavaScript runtime completely drains the Microtask Queue (Promises, queueMicrotask, MutationObserver) before picking the next macrotask.

questions.question: What is the primary technical benefit of using the CSS 'contain' property (e.g., contain: content)?
options: It forces all nested elements to display as inline blocks
It isolates the subtree so changes inside do not trigger layout or paint recalculations outside the subtree
It prevents children from inheriting CSS variables
It automatically optimizes image loading across the document
questions.answer: It isolates the subtree so changes inside do not trigger layout or paint recalculations outside the subtree
questions.explanation: CSS containment informs the browser rendering engine that an element's subtree is independent of the rest of the page, limiting recalculation scope for layout, style, paint, and size.

questions.question: In React 18/19, what does wrapping a state update in 'startTransition' tell the scheduler?
options: To execute the update synchronously and block all user inputs
To mark the update as a non-urgent transition that can be interrupted by urgent inputs like typing or clicking
To memoize the component's rendered output in localStorage
To run the component inside a dedicated Web Worker
questions.answer: To mark the update as a non-urgent transition that can be interrupted by urgent inputs like typing or clicking
questions.explanation: startTransition categorizes updates into non-urgent transitions, enabling React Concurrent Mode to keep the UI interactive and avoid input stutter during large tree re-renders.

questions.question: What happens when you pass a primitive value to 'Object.freeze()' in JavaScript?
options: It throws a TypeError
It converts the primitive to an immutable Symbol
In ES6+, it simply returns the primitive value without error
It creates a deep proxy copy of the primitive
questions.answer: In ES6+, it simply returns the primitive value without error
questions.explanation: In ES5, passing a primitive to Object.freeze threw a TypeError; however, in ES6+ specifications, primitives are treated as already immutable and returned unchanged.

questions.question: Which TypeScript utility type constructs a type with all properties of Type set to optional?
options: Readonly<T>
Partial<T>
Required<T>
Record<T, any>
questions.explanation: Partial<T> maps over every key in T and applies the optional modifier '?'.

questions.question: Which Core Web Vital metric measures visual stability by calculating the sum of unexpected layout shift scores?
options: LCP
INP
CLS
TTFB
questions.explanation: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) measures the visual stability of a page by summing layout shift scores during the session.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'useLayoutEffect' and 'useEffect' in React?
options: useLayoutEffect runs on the server, whereas useEffect runs on the client
useLayoutEffect fires synchronously after all DOM mutations but before the browser paints
useLayoutEffect cannot have a cleanup function
useLayoutEffect runs asynchronously inside a requestIdleCallback
questions.answer: useLayoutEffect fires synchronously after all DOM mutations but before the browser paints
questions.explanation: useLayoutEffect runs synchronously immediately after DOM mutations, preventing visual flickers when measuring DOM layout before paint.

questions.question: When configuring HTTP caching for immutable hashed assets (e.g. /bundle.a8b1c.js), what is the optimal Cache-Control value?
options: Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store
Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable
Cache-Control: private, must-revalidate
Cache-Control: s-maxage=0
questions.explanation: The 'immutable' directive indicates to modern browsers and CDNs that the response will never change while fresh, avoiding conditional 304 revalidations.

questions.question: How does React Fiber prevent blocking the main browser thread during massive updates?
options: It compiles JSX directly into WebAssembly modules
It breaks rendering work into incremental fiber units that can pause, yield, and resume across frame deadlines
It disables all CSS animations during render
It offloads React elements to Service Workers
questions.answer: It breaks rendering work into incremental fiber units that can pause, yield, and resume across frame deadlines
questions.explanation: Fiber represents each component as a unit of work with child, sibling, and return pointers, allowing React to yield control back to the browser event loop.

questions.question: What is the danger of relying on Array index as the 'key' prop for dynamically reordered lists in React?
options: It causes TypeScript compile errors
It breaks component state association, causing inputs/animations to attach to incorrect items upon deletion or reordering
It disables virtual DOM diffing altogether
It causes memory leaks in the browser garbage collector
questions.answer: It breaks component state association, causing inputs/animations to attach to incorrect items upon deletion or reordering
questions.explanation: Index keys cause React to match elements by position rather than identity. When elements shift or delete, internal state and uncontrolled DOM nodes remain bound to the position index.
